card_notes.text: Walt and Ines are old friends.

characters.name: Ines Calder
characters.appearance: Narrow-faced, with a grey streak at one temple and a dark coat always worn with the collar turned up.
characters.sketch: A private investigator who has outlasted her patience and kept her curiosity.

wants.text: to be left out of other people's trouble

characters.fear: Being useful only to people who cannot be trusted.
characters.flaw: She refuses to admit she needs anyone, even when the work needs a second pair of hands.

values.text: telling the truth to a paying client

behaviors.tendency: hum and straighten whatever is nearest

characters.competence: Reads rooms and records faster than anyone.
characters.vulnerability: She cannot leave a locked door alone.
characters.speech: Dry and spare, with questions disguised as remarks.
characters.history: Spent years as a clerk before going private.

characters.name: Walt Orsolo
characters.appearance: Broad and stoop-shouldered, with a bartender's forearms and a nose broken twice.
characters.sketch: A bar owner who knows everyone's business and has never repeated any of it.

wants.text: to keep what he has built

characters.fear: Losing the bar, and with it his place on the street.
characters.flaw: He avoids confrontation until it is too late to avoid anything else.

behaviors.tendency: busy himself polishing glasses and change the subject
talk easily about the old days

characters.competence: Remembers every face and every debt.
characters.vulnerability: He is easily shamed by being thought weak.
characters.history: Has run the bar for thirty years.

world.name: Marrow Bay
world.era_and_technology: A mid-century port city of steam cranes, telephones and typewriters, with no computers.
world.everyday_life: Everyone on the waterfront pays someone, and favors and receipts are the real currency; nobody speaks plainly about either.
world.history: The port boomed during the war and has been fought over ever since.

places.name: The Lantern Bar
places.description: A low-ceilinged dockside bar with a worn bar-top and a back room.
places.effect: Conversation stops when certain people walk in, and the regulars sit with their backs to the wall.

places.name: Quay Street
places.description: The long street of shops and bars along the harbor.
places.effect: Everyone on it can see who goes in where, so nothing stays private.

objects.name: The burial fund ledger
objects.description: A thin cloth-bound book, the Mutual's official record of its burial fund.
objects.significance: If it were opened, it would show whether the fund holds anything.

powers.name: The Harbor Mutual
powers.nature: A burial society for dockworkers' widows that now collects monthly dues from nearly every business on the waterfront.
powers.hold: It collects in person and can make a business's books look bad until the owner sells.
powers.felt: Owners dread the first Friday of every month and lower their voices when its collectors pass.

rules.statement: The Mutual's dues are passed on each month to an official at the Customs House.
rules.cost: Anyone who says so aloud risks the Mutual's retaliation and loses the official's protection.
rules.when_broken: The Mutual and the official both lose their income, and whoever exposed them becomes a target.

rules.statement: The Mutual's dues pay for burials and widows' pensions.
rules.cost: Owners who withhold dues are accused of shortchanging widows.
rules.when_broken: Nothing visible happens; the belief is simply repeated.

terms.meaning: the monthly payment every waterfront business makes to the Mutual
